library_preparation_preflight.summary: Standard scaffold suffices (Jackson/http-client-jdk resolve transitively via testImplementation, no Docker/network needed); the only risk is tests silently skipping the Jackson response mapping if pointed at the real API instead of a local fake endpoint.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Point VoyageAiEmbeddingModel.builder().baseUrl(...) / VoyageAiScoringModel.builder().baseUrl(...) at a local fake HTTP endpoint (e.g. com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer, the pattern already used in ~44 other TCK tests in this repo) instead of the real https://api.voyageai.com default — the client only validates apiKey is non-blank (no real auth), so any placeholder string works for both apiKey and modelName. Have the fake endpoint return canned JSON matching Voyage's actual snake_case wire format so the reflective Jackson mapping is actually exercised: for POST /embeddings -> {"object":...,"data":[{"object":...,"embedding":[...],"index":0}],"model":...,"usage":{"total_tokens":...}} (EmbeddingResponse/EmbeddingResponse.EmbeddingData); for POST /rerank -> {"object":...,"data":[{"object":...,"relevance_score":0.9,"index":0}],"model":...,"usage":{"total_tokens":...}} (RerankResponse/RerankResponse.RerankData). Exercise both VoyageAiEmbeddingModel.embed/embedAll (via /embeddings) and VoyageAiScoringModel.scoreAll (via /rerank) if practical, since they hit distinct response DTOs. A plain JSON array for the embedding field is sufficient; no need to cover the base64-encoded alternative form.
risks: If the generated test exercises the model against the real default baseUrl with a placeholder API key, the call fails on auth/network before ever reaching the JSON response deserialization — producing a passing-looking test that exercises none of the Jackson reflection this issue exists to cover.
